newsitem.title: USA: ComEd Zion nuke seen reduced through summer.
newsitem.headline: ComEd Zion nuke seen reduced through summer.

text.p: Commonwealth Edison Co's 1,040 megawatt (MW) Zion nuclear power unit 1 will operate at less than half of its rated capacity through the summer, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Wednesday.
Commonwealth Edison plans to operate the unit at near 40 percent of capacity until May, when a three-week surveillance outage will be performed, the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
Following the surveillance outage, the unit will return to about 40 percent power and will remain on line through the summer but will coast down to a refueling outage, the NRC said.
Zion 1, located in Zion, Ill., was operating at 41 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday.
A company spokesman was not immediately available for comment on the reduced output at the unit.
The adjacent 1,040 Zion nuclear power unit 2 has been shut since Sept 18 for scheduled refueling and maintenance.
The NRC said Wednesday Zion 2 was expected to resume electricity production Feb 28.
ComEd is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
